Let \(A_n=1+a_n\). Then
\[
A_{n+1}=1+a_{n+1}=1+\frac{n}{a_n+1}=1+\frac n{A_n},\qquad A_1=2.
\]

We prove by induction that for all \(n\ge 6\),
\[
\sqrt n+\frac15<A_n<\sqrt n+\frac45.
\]

Base: \(A_6=1+\frac{20}{11}=\frac{31}{11}\), and
\[
\sqrt6+\frac15<\frac{31}{11}<\sqrt6+\frac45.
\]

Assume \(s+\frac15<A_n<s+\frac45\), where \(s=\sqrt n\). Then
\[
A_{n+1}>1+\frac{s^2}{s+\frac45}
=s+\frac15+\frac{16}{25s+20}.
\]
For \(n\ge 6\), one checks
\[
\frac{16}{25s+20}>\frac1{\sqrt{n+1}+s},
\]
so \(A_{n+1}>\sqrt{n+1}+\frac15\).

Similarly,
\[
A_{n+1}<1+\frac{s^2}{s+\frac15}
=s+\frac45+\frac1{25s+5}
<\sqrt{n+1}+\frac45.
\]
Thus the claim holds.

For \(n=2008\):
\[
A_{2008}>\sqrt{2008}+\frac15>44.8+\frac15=45,
\]
since \(44.8^2=2007.04<2008\). Also
\[
A_{2008}<\sqrt{2008}+\frac45<45+\frac45=45.8,
\]
so
\[
a_{2008}=A_{2008}-1
\]
gives
\[
44<a_{2008}<45.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\boxed{44}
\]
